newsitem.title: THAILAND: Support fund begins buying Thai stocks - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Support fund begins buying Thai stocks - brokers.

text.p: An initial tranche of a planned 50 billion baht ($1.92 billion) Thai stock market support fund began buying shares on Wednesday, brokers said.
Fund administrator Krung Thai Bank Plc declined to confirm that the support fund was buying on Wednesday, but said it was able to begin using fund money to buy stocks from today.

"According to the Thai Bankers Association's resolution, one billion becomes available on Thursday but Krung Thai Bank is allowed to start buying today. We can place orders now and settle in up to three working days," Krung Thai Bank Senior Vice President Dusit Tengniyopm told Reuters.
Brokers said they believed the fund's purchase of blue chip stocks was partly responsible for a sharp morning surge in the Thai market, and increased trading volumes.

The SET Index, which plunged to eight-year lows last week, was up 23.82 points or 4.13 percent, to 600.92 by 0519 GMT. The blue chip SET 50 Index was up 23.83 points, or 5.29 percent to 44.37. Turnover was 3.55 billion by 0519 GMT.

"A total of around one billion baht of a total market support fund has entered the market today. The fund is buying all the blue chip shares," said Somchai Trairattanapirom, vice presdent at Sitca Investment and Securities Plc.

The local commerical bank association, the Thai Bankers Association, is collecting money from its members to help support the Thai stock market which has been one of the world's worst performing exchanges over the last year.
Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has said that up to 50 billion baht may become available and that the downside risk of the market was now limited.

Several support funds have been launched in the past 18 months, none of which have had a significant impact on the downtrend of a market in which sentiment has been hurt by Thailand's worsening economic fundamentals.
